speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you tell me how long this has been going on and if the pain wakes you up at night?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: The mechanism of injury suggests an acute traumatic event. Did you notice any deformity of the finger immediately after the pull, or were you able to continue playing?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Avulsion fracture of the distal phalanx extensor insertion).

The history of forced flexion while extending the finger, combined with the inability to actively extend the distal joint and the finger resting in extension, confirms a disruption of the extensor mechanism at the DIP. I do not require further imaging as the clinical presentation is classic for this injury.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
